High river levels today have led to  flooding. A small amount of rain (5mm) has fallen in the last 24 hours. Flooding is affecting low lying land, roads, cycle tracks and footpaths close to the river. Flooding of Golf Links Road and Moreton Common Road has occurred. Ditches around Fort Holiday Park will struggle to drain while river levels are high. Only a small amount of rain is forecast over Friday 20/11/2026 and Saturday 21/11/2026. River levels and flood risk should begin to reduce in Alverstone, and Sandown over the next 48 hours. Further rain is forecast (up to 20mm each day) from Sunday 22/11/2026 until Tuesday 24/11/2026. If this affects the Eastern Yar this may cause the river to rise again.  We are  monitoring rainfall and river levels and will ensure the river is kept free of reported blockages. Consider activating any flood protection products you may have. Including in Alverstone. This message will be updated by 21/11/2026 13:00.

items.description: The River Bure, Spixworth Beck and surrounding Becks
items.message:
High river levels today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible on Friday 20 November .
Locations most affected will be low lying roads and riverside areas between Horsford and Crostwick on the Spixworth Beck, and Corpusty, Saxthorpe, Itteringham, Ingworth, Aylsham and Burgh-next-Aylsham on the Bure. The river levels in the Spixworth Beck are expected to peak soon, and then fall by mid-afternoon today, Friday 20th November. We are not expecting the situation to escalate, or to issue any further warning messages at this time.
We are monitoring rainfall and river levels .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Saturday 21 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.message: Flooding is possible today, Friday 20th November, and for the next few days. This is due to tide locking, where high tides restrict normal drainage of the river out to sea. We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak compared to published tide tables. We are closely monitoring the situation. Take care and avoid walking, cycling, or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 10am on Saturday 21st November, or as the situation changes.
